sentence: Hydroxychloroquine is a medicine used to treat rheumatoid arthritis, lupus and some skin conditions.
note: NHS search text: used to treat conditions like rheumatoid arthritis, lupus and some skin conditions.

sentence: It is available only on prescription.
note: NHS search text: only available on prescription.

sentence: MedlinePlus places it in a group of medicines called antimalarials and also describes it as an antirheumatic drug.
note: MedlinePlus excerpt: class of drugs called antimalarials; also an antirheumatic.

sentence: The NHS describes it as a disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drug (DMARD) that calms the immune system.
note: NHS Common questions summary: DMARD that calms your immune system.

sentence: It is not a painkiller, although pain may ease as symptoms improve.
note: NHS Common questions summary.

sentence: How hydroxychloroquine calms the immune system has not been fully worked out.
note: Reviews say mechanism not yet fully elucidated; search summary blended two PMC reviews. DOUBTFUL attribution.

sentence: Reviews describe it building up inside small cell compartments called lysosomes and disrupting how immune cells process and present antigens.
note: Reviews: enters lysosomes, raises pH and disrupts antigen processing.

sentence: The NHS says benefit comes slowly, and it can take several weeks before improvement is noticed in conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis and lupus.
note: NHS text says 6 to 12 weeks; number deliberately left out.

sentence: The NHS advises that feeling better is not on its own a reason to stop treatment.
note: NHS main-page summary: advises not to stop just because you feel better. DOUBTFUL: summary paraphrase.

sentence: Common side effects listed by the NHS include stomach ache, feeling or being sick, loss of appetite, diarrhoea, headache and an itchy rash.
note: NHS side effects page summary.

sentence: Mood changes are also listed.
note: NHS side effects summary.

sentence: Blurred vision can occur when treatment starts, and the NHS says to avoid driving, cycling or using machinery until vision is back to normal.
note: NHS summary: do not drive, ride a bike or use machinery.

sentence: Serious but uncommon effects listed by the NHS include a severe allergic reaction, severe skin reactions, liver problems and damage to the retina of the eye.
note: NHS side effects summary.

sentence: The NHS also lists low blood sugar, unusual bruising or infections, muscle weakness, and changes in mood or thinking, including thoughts of self-harm.
note: NHS side effects summary.

sentence: The NHS says to call 999 if the lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell, or if breathing becomes very difficult.
note: NHS summary: Call 999 now if lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swollen or breathing very difficult.

sentence: For other serious side effects the NHS points people to NHS 111.
note: NHS main-page summary: think serious side effects, call NHS 111. DOUBTFUL: from summary.

sentence: For thoughts of self-harm, 999 is for immediate danger, NHS 111 has a mental health option, and Samaritans is free on 116 123 at any time.
note: Site signposting rule for mental-health content, not from the retrieved text.

sentence: Hydroxychloroquine can, rarely, cause changes in the retina, the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, after long-term use.
note: Lupus UK: in rare cases HCQ can cause changes in the retina after long-term use.

sentence: Retinopathy can be silent at first, so eye checks are used to find it before symptoms appear.
note: PMC review summary: often silent early on.

sentence: The retinal changes are largely irreversible, which is why early detection matters.
note: RCOphth guideline: largely irreversible; Lupus UK: generally permanent.

sentence: Severe damage to the central retina can cause permanent sight loss.
note: Eye-screening leaflet summary. DOUBTFUL: attributed from blended summary.

sentence: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists says extra risk factors, such as high daily dose, tamoxifen or reduced kidney function, can justify earlier eye monitoring.
note: RCOphth summary of risk factors.

sentence: Its guidance describes monitoring with retinal imaging such as optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans.
note: RCOphth 2020: OCT and widefield FAF imaging.

sentence: The Royal College no longer asks for a routine baseline eye test for people starting treatment.
note: RCOphth December 2020 revision.

sentence: Versus Arthritis advises telling an optician about hydroxychloroquine and having regular eye check-ups.
note: Versus Arthritis: check-up with optician; yearly frequency left out.

sentence: NRAS advises contacting the GP or specialist team about any change in vision while taking it.
note: NRAS summary.

sentence: Versus Arthritis says to report new eye symptoms to a doctor straight away.
note: Versus Arthritis summary.

sentence: The Royal College says the decision to stop treatment belongs to the prescribing doctor rather than the eye specialist.
note: RCOphth: inappropriate for ophthalmologists to stop; prescriber decides.

sentence: The NHS lists a past allergic reaction to hydroxychloroquine or similar medicines, such as quinine, as a reason it may not be suitable.
note: NHS who-can summary.

sentence: It also lists some eye, liver, kidney, heart and blood conditions, psoriasis and porphyria as needing care.
note: NHS summary. DOUBTFUL: list taken from summary, wording may differ.

sentence: Versus Arthritis says it is not usually prescribed to people with maculopathy, a problem with the central part of the retina.
note: Versus Arthritis summary.

sentence: The NHS says it is not considered an immunosuppressant but may lower white blood cell numbers, which can make infections more likely.
note: NHS Common questions summary.

sentence: Hospital guidance generally says treatment can continue through pregnancy, and the specialist team is told early if pregnancy is planned or happens.
note: Several NHS shared-care sheets. DOUBTFUL: older sheets conflict.

sentence: Some guidance describes it as compatible with breastfeeding, although small amounts pass into breast milk.
note: East and North Herts leaflet. DOUBTFUL: older sheets say otherwise.

sentence: Sheets from different hospitals differ in age and wording on pregnancy, so the specialist team gives advice for each person.
note: Synthesis of conflicting local sheets. DOUBTFUL.

sentence: The NHS says alcohol can be drunk while taking hydroxychloroquine.
note: NHS Common questions summary.

sentence: The NHS advises telling the doctor about all other medicines, herbal remedies, vitamins and supplements before starting.
note: NHS Common questions summary.

sentence: Long-term users usually have regular blood tests and eye checks.
note: NHS side effects summary.
